actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and inspect roots
If roots are mushy or smelly, cut off rotted roots
Repot into pot 1-2 inches bigger with drainage holes and fresh well-draining mix
Water again only when top 1-2 inches of soil dry
Cut vines back hard, removing dead sections, just below nodes
Move plant to bright, indirect light
Propagate healthy node cuttings in water or moist soil
Plant rooted cuttings back into the pot

reason: The answer attributes wilting to excessive vine length and a root-bound pot and calls a hard cut-back plus repotting the key step, matching the confirmed trim-and-repot fix; nothing in it is harmful.
